mostWorthwhile.text: Joining the eye front to the retina was most worthwhile because it showed the whole path from focused light to signals heading toward the brain.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the iris was clear but fairly predictable: the opening and its light-control job had already been shown.

surprise.text: The retina was a curved sheet connected to nerve cells whose fibres gathered into the optic nerve. That made the outgoing route clearer.

arbitrary.text: None felt especially arbitrary; the pictures and goals explained the pairings, although the last two combinations were the only available actions.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see how the brain uses signals from the eye, though this chapter's choices became predictable toward the end.
